design.allocation: one 512 MiB device slab bumped per call, plus one pinned staging buffer for host transfers: the device counterpart of the CPU arena
design.build: python setup_cuda.py build_ext --inplace (nvcc, --fmad=false to match the CPU build's -ffp-contract=off, no fast math)
design.drop_in: every entry point of tunnel_guard._native exists; the four ported ones run on the device and the rest forward to the CPU module by name
design.selected_by: detector config key native_backend = cuda; the default remains cpu, and an unsatisfiable cuda request raises instead of falling back
design.small_calls: calls below the documented size thresholds are served by the CPU kernel, because the transfer costs more than the work

decisions.comparison: scripts/compare_runs.py, CPU backend against CUDA backend

equivalence.method: the replay runs on the CPU kernels and the arguments of every real call are captured, then the same call is evaluated on both backends and compared byte for byte

host.cpu: AMD EPYC 7742 pinned to eight logical CPUs (taskset 0-7)
host.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080, 16 GB, driver 590.48.01, compute capability 8.9
host.note: The deployment stand is an i7-9700E with an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. The rented card is the same architecture and the same 1:64 FP64 ratio; the rented CPU is not the stand's.

limitations: Equivalence is established on one recording (201 scans). The ported kernels are element-wise or integer-exact by construction, but no second recording has been run.

The device kernels were compared on the arguments real frames produce; inputs outside that population (a voxel key outside the packed 21-bit field, or a call below the size threshold) are served by the CPU kernel rather than being handled on the device.
No target-stand measurement exists. The rented host has the same GPU architecture and FP64 ratio, but a different CPU.

The device path is deterministic by construction (stable radix sort, integer atomic counters, per-element arithmetic with --fmad=false), but run-to-run repetition of the device path was not measured separately.
The remaining 421 ms of the frame is Open3D's plane proposals (280 ms) and kiss-ICP (141 ms), neither of which is in this extension.

larger_costs_that_are_not_ours.open3d_segment_plane: 280 ms/frame (1,037 calls per 30 scans; mean 8.1 ms, p50 1.12 ms, max 42.5 ms)

not_ported.measured_cpu_cost_per_frame: about 95 ms of the 737 ms frame, split between normal_statistics 21.4, density_graph 19.5 (both already threaded on the CPU), cluster_objects 7.6, ground_profile 4.5, voxel_counts 4.2, mask_apply 3.1, component_labels 1.4

scope: Optional CUDA backend for the detector's native kernels; no decision changed.

timing_ms_per_frame.entry_point_note: p50 of the per-call cost over 30 scans; the four ported kernels sum to about 25 ms of the saving on their own.
timing_ms_per_frame.first_call_note: The first device call in a process pays context creation, the pinned staging allocation and cub setup: range_indices' first call measured 168 ms, so a deployment must warm the backend before the stream starts.
timing_ms_per_frame.panel: 201 real scans of doubleT_obstacle, CPU backend against CUDA backend, same pinned cpuset
timing_ms_per_frame.why_more_than_the_sum: The device backend also removes those kernels' threads from the eight pinned CPUs, which shortens the CPU-bound stages that share them (Open3D's plane proposals and kiss-ICP are single-threaded but contend for the same cores and memory bandwidth).
